verses.zh: 论大马士革的默示：看哪，大马士革已被废弃，不再为城，必变作乱堆。
verses.en: This is an oracle[NOTE:1] about Damascus:“Look, Damascus is no longer a city,it is a heap of ruins!
notes: See note at Isa 13:1.

verses.zh: 亚罗珥的城邑已被撇弃，必成为牧羊之处；羊在那里躺卧，无人惊吓。
verses.en: The cities of Aroer are abandoned.[NOTE:1] They will be used for herds,which will lie down there in peace.[NOTE:2]
notes: Three cities are known by this name in the OT: (1) an Aroer located near the Arnon, (2) an Aroer in Ammon, and (3) an Aroer of Judah. (See BDB 792-93 s.v. עֲרֹעֵר, and HALOT 883 s.v. II עֲרוֹעֵר.) There is no mention of an Aroer in Syrian territory. For this reason some want to emend the text here to עֲזֻבוֹת עָרַיהָ עֲדֵי עַד (ʿazuvot ʿarayha ʿade ʿad, “her cities are permanently abandoned”). However, Aroer near the Arnon was taken by Israel and later conquered by the Syrians. (See Josh 12:2; 13:9, 16; Judg 11:26; 2 Kgs 10:33). This oracle pertains to Israel as well as Syria (note v. 3), so it is possible that this is a reference to Israelite and/or Syrian losses in Transjordan.
Heb “and they lie down, and there is no one scaring [them].”

verses.zh: 以法莲不再有保障；大马士革不再有国权；亚兰所剩下的必像以色列人的荣耀消灭一样。这是万军之耶和华说的。
verses.en: Fortified cities will disappear from Ephraim,and Damascus will lose its kingdom.[NOTE:1] The survivors in Syriawill end up like the splendor of the Israelites,”says the Lord of Heaven’s Armies.
notes: Heb “and kingship from Damascus”; cf. NASB “And sovereignty from Damascus.”

verses.zh: 到那日，雅各的荣耀必至枵薄；他肥胖的身体必渐瘦弱。
verses.en: “At that time[NOTE:1] Jacob’s splendor will be greatly diminished,[NOTE:2] and he will become skin and bones.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “in that day” (so KJV). The verb that introduces this verse serves as a discourse particle and is untranslated; see note on “in the future” in 2:2.
Heb “will be tiny.”
Heb “and the fatness of his flesh will be made lean.”

verses.zh: 就必像收割的人收敛禾稼，用手割取穗子，又像人在利乏音谷拾取遗落的穗子。
verses.en: It will be as when one gathers the grain harvest and his hand gleans the ear of grain.It will be like one gathering the ears of grainin the Valley of Rephaim.

verses.zh: 其间所剩下的不多，好像人打橄榄树―在尽上的枝梢上只剩两三个果子；在多果树的旁枝上只剩四五个果子。这是耶和华―以色列的　神说的。
verses.en: There will be some left behind,as when an olive tree is beaten—two or three ripe olives remain toward the very top,four or five on its fruitful branches,”says the Lord God of Israel.

verses.zh: 当那日，人必仰望造他们的主，眼目重看以色列的圣者。
verses.en: At that time[NOTE:1] men will trust in their Creator;[NOTE:2] they will depend on[NOTE:3] the Holy One of Israel.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “in that day” (so ASV, NASB, NIV); KJV “At that day.”
Heb “man will gaze toward his maker.”
Heb “his eyes will look toward.”
See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.

verses.zh: 他们必不仰望祭坛，就是自己手所筑的，也不重看自己指头所做的，无论是木偶是日像。
verses.en: They will no longer trust in[NOTE:1] the altars their hands made,or depend on the Asherah poles and incense altars their fingers made.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “he will not gaze toward.”
Heb “and that which his fingers made he will not see, the Asherah poles and the incense altars.”

verses.zh: 在那日，他们的坚固城必像树林中和山顶上所撇弃的地方，就是从前在以色列人面前被人撇弃的。这样，地就荒凉了。
verses.en: At that time[NOTE:1] their fortified cities will be like the abandoned summits of the Amorites,[NOTE:2] which they abandoned because of the Israelites;there will be desolation.
notes: Heb “in that day” (so KJV).

The Hebrew text reads literally, “like the abandonment of the wooded height and the top one.” The following relative clause appears to allude back to the Israelite conquest of the land, so it seems preferable to emend הַחֹרֶשׁ וְהָאָמִיר (hakhoresh vehaʾamir, “the wooded height and the top one”) to חֹרֵשֵׁי הָאֱמֹרִי (khoreshe haʾemori, “[like the abandonment] of the wooded heights of the Amorites”).

verses.zh: 因你忘记救你的　神，不记念你能力的磐石；所以，你栽上佳美的树秧子，插上异样的栽子。
verses.en: For you ignore[NOTE:1] the God who rescues you;you pay no attention to your strong protector.[NOTE:2] So this is what happens:You cultivate beautiful plantsand plant exotic vines.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “you have forgotten” (so NAB, NIV, NRSV).
Heb “and the rocky cliff of your strength you do not remember.”

Heb “a vine, a strange one.” The substantival adjective זָר (zar) functions here as an appositional genitive. It could refer to a cultic plant of some type, associated with a pagan rite. But it is more likely that it refers to an exotic, or imported, type of vine, one that is foreign (i.e., “strange”) to Israel.

verses.zh: 栽种的日子，你周围圈上篱笆，又到早晨使你所种的开花；但在愁苦极其伤痛的日子，所收割的都飞去了。
verses.en: The day you begin cultivating, you do what you can to make it grow;[NOTE:1] the morning you begin planting, you do what you can to make it sprout.Yet the harvest will disappear[NOTE:2] in the day of diseaseand incurable pain.
notes: Heb “in the day of your planting you [?].” The precise meaning of the verb תְּשַׂגְשֵׂגִי (tesagsegi) is unclear. It is sometimes derived from שׂוּג/סוּג (sug, “to fence in”; see BDB 691 s.v. II סוּג). In this case one could translate “you build a protective fence.” However, the parallelism is tighter if one derives the form from שָׂגָא/שָׂגָה (sagaʾ/sagah, “to grow”); see J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah (NICOT), 1:351, n. 4. For this verb, see BDB 960 s.v. שָׂגָא.

The Hebrew text has, “a heap of harvest.” However, better sense is achieved if נֵד (ned, “heap”) is emended to a verb. Options include נַד (nad, Qal perfect third masculine singular from נָדַד [nadad, “flee, depart”]), נָדַד (Qal perfect third masculine singular from נָדַד), נֹדֵד (noded, Qal active participle from נָדַד), and נָד (nad, Qal perfect third masculine singular, or participle masculine singular, from נוּד [nud, “wander, flutter”]). See BDB 626 s.v. נוּד and HALOT 672 s.v. I נדד. One could translate literally: “[the harvest] departs,” or “[the harvest] flies away.”

verses.zh: 唉！多民哄嚷，好像海浪匉訇；列邦奔腾，好像猛水滔滔；
verses.en: Beware, you many nations massing together,[NOTE:1] those who make a commotion as loud as the roaring of the sea’s waves.[NOTE:2] Beware, you people making such an uproar,[NOTE:3] those who make an uproar as loud as the roaring of powerful waves.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “Woe [to] the massing of the many nations.”
Heb “like the loud noise of the seas, they make a loud noise.”
Heb “the uproar of the peoples.”
Heb “like the uproar of mighty waters they are in an uproar.”

verses.zh: 列邦奔腾，好像多水滔滔；但　神斥责他们，他们就远远逃避，又被追赶，如同山上的风前糠，又如暴风前的旋风土。
verses.en: Though these people make an uproar as loud as the roaring of powerful waves,[NOTE:1] when he shouts at[NOTE:2] them, they will flee to a distant land,driven before the wind like dead weeds on the hillsor like dead thistles[NOTE:3] before a strong gale.
notes: Heb “the peoples are in an uproar like the uproar of mighty waters.”

Or “rebukes.” The verb and related noun are used in theophanies of God’s battle cry, which terrifies his enemies. See, for example, Pss 18:15; 76:7; 106:9; Isa 50:2; Nah 1:4, and A. Caquot, TDOT 3:49-53.
Or perhaps “tumbleweed” (NAB, NIV, CEV); KJV “like a rolling thing.”

verses.zh: 到晚上有惊吓，未到早晨他们就没有了。这是掳掠我们之人所得的分，是抢夺我们之人的报应。
verses.en: In the evening there is sudden terror;[NOTE:1] by morning they vanish.[NOTE:2] This is the fate of those who try to plunder us,the destiny of those who try to loot us![NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “at the time of evening, look, sudden terror.”
Heb “before morning he is not.”
Heb “this is the portion of those who plunder us, and the lot of those who loot us.”
